title: Benny and the Wishing Star
markdown:
The sun was painting the sky with sleepy purples and soft oranges over the Whispering Woods. In his cozy den, Benny the bear cub yawned a big rumbling yawn, his velvet ears twitching. Benny loved his woods, especially when the fireflies started to wink their little lights and the air smelled like warm honey and blooming clover. It was a perfectly peaceful evening, the kind that made your toes wiggle with happiness.

“Almost time for dreamland, Benny-boo,” a tiny voice chimed, flitting near his nose like a little puff of rainbow. It was Floss, a cupcake fairy with wings that shimmered like strawberry frosting and a laugh like tiny silver bells. “But first. The Wishing Cake needs its starry crown.”

Benny blinked his sleepy eyes, the colour of warm milk. Oh yes. The Wishing Cake. Once a year, on this very night, a special cake appeared in the moonlit meadow, and if a frosting star was placed on its highest point before the very last sliver of sun disappeared, it granted a special wish for everyone in the Whispering Woods. This year the special star was waiting, just a little bit melty and warm, on the very tippy-top of Sleepy Willow Hill.

“Is it melty yet?” Benny asked, his voice a little wobbly, like his legs sometimes were when he was extra excited or a little bit worried. He really hoped it wasn’t too melty.

Floss giggled, as light as dandelion fluff. “Just a little bit, Benny. Like a warm hug from the sun. But don’t you worry your fuzzy head. We have to hurry. And we will be super-duper careful.” She held out a small shimmering frosting star, shaped like a perfect twinkle. It was soft to the touch and smelled faintly of sweet vanilla and happy thoughts.

Benny carefully took the star, his big paws as gentle as if he were holding a precious butterfly. “Okay, Floss. Let’s go make a wish that makes everyone happy.”

They started up Sleepy Willow Hill. Benny padded softly on the forest floor, his furry body a warm shadow in the fading light. Floss fluttered beside him, her wings leaving tiny trails of sparkle like captured moonlight. Benny’s paws made a soft shush-shush upon the leafy trail. The path was soft with fallen leaves, like the woods whispering secrets. Benny hummed a little tune, a soft low song his Mama sang to help him fall asleep, and Floss hummed along with her own happy high-pitched tune, her wings making tiny rainbows in the twilight air.

“Look, Benny,” Floss whispered, pointing a tiny finger towards a patch of flowers. “Moon-daisies. They smell like sweet dreams are made of. Take a big sniff.”

Benny took a deep happy breath. Yes, they smelled lovely, and so did the wild honeysuckle climbing the ancient trees, its perfume mixing with the fresh clean smell of the forest. The air was warm and soft, like a cuddly blanket being tucked around the woods. It was so peaceful it almost made Benny want to curl up and nap right there.

They walked and walked, the hill winding around them like a sleepy green snake stretching. Benny’s tummy rumbled a tiny polite rumble. He really wished he had one of his Mama’s yummy honey sandwiches. But the precious frosting star was in his paws, cool and sweet, and he knew he had to be brave and steady all the way. He imagined the happy faces of all his friends in the woods when their wish came true.

As they climbed higher, the path grew a little steeper, and the last of the sun’s golden rays tiptoed away behind the tallest trees, painting the sky in even softer deeper colours. Benny’s legs started to feel a little tired, like wobbly jelly. And oh dear, the frosting star in his paws wobbled, just a little bit. Wobble, wobble. He held his breath. Then a single tiny drop of the special frosting star slipped from its point and began falling, falling, falling.

“Oh no. My little star,” Benny whispered.

But Floss, who was always looking and always thinking, spotted something wonderful just ahead. It was a patch of the softest, most wonderfully green moss she had ever seen, glistening like a carpet of emeralds in the gentle moonlight. It looked like a little sleepy pillow, just waiting for something precious to rest upon it. She remembered her wise grandmother fairy, who had taught her all about the secrets of the Whispering Woods, telling stories about how the softest moss could hold even the most delicate things safe and sound, like tiny treasures tucked away in a chest.

“Benny. Over here,” Floss chirped, still cheerful and full of bright hope. “Let’s rest the star on this comfy moss. It’s like a little bed for wishes, the comfiest bed in the whole wide woods. It will keep it safe and sound.”

Benny, with a relieved sigh that puffed out his cheeks, carefully lowered the frosting star onto the cool velvety moss. It settled down with a soft little thump. And the tiny drop of frosting that had fallen landed right beside it, and instead of melting away into nothing, it shimmered and twinkled, catching the moonlight like a tiny captured star-drop. It looked like a perfect tiny dewdrop, reflecting the silvery moon and all the twinkling stars above.

They looked at the frosting star, resting so peacefully, and then at the little frosting dewdrop, which seemed to be smiling back at them, and then at each other. They had not quite made it to the very, very tippy-top of the hill, where the Wishing Cake was waiting. But the star was safe, and the little frosting drop seemed to be showing them that it was happy too. The Wishing Cake in the meadow below would understand. The magic was not lost. It was just resting, in a beautiful new way.

A quiet sigh of contentment floated between them, a soft sound like rustling leaves. The woods were hushed now, the crickets singing their softest most peaceful lullabies. The last of the twilight colours had faded, leaving the gentle comforting glow of the moon and the countless sparkling stars. Benny felt his eyes grow heavy, like little sleepy curtains drawing closed. Floss snuggled onto Benny’s fuzzy ear, her iridescent wings tucked neatly beside her. Everything was just right, perfectly peaceful, and soon they both drifted into the sweetest sleepy dreams, the frosting star shining on its mossy bed like a second, smaller moon.
characters: Benny (a bear cub), Floss (the cupcake fairy)
author: StoryGen Community
